land.text: Cliopatria's 540 shape of Gwent, cut out of the sub-Roman Brythonic lands: south-east Wales between the Wye and the Usk

predecessors.note: The page has Gwent form after the Roman withdrawal from Britain in the 5th century and gives no founding year; 540 is Cliopatria's start. The infobox lists Roman Britain and the Kingdom of Morgannwg as predecessors.

land.text: what remained of Gwent in 1074, taken by Caradog ap Gruffudd from Cadwgan ap Meurig

successors.note: Gwent page, 1074: Caradog takes control of what remains of Gwent from Cadwgan; the infobox names the Kingdom of Morgannwg as successor. Morgannwg then held the land until the Normans took it (Gwent page 1081; Norman invasion page: a castle at Caerleon by 1086).

Page: at Hereford in 926 Athelstan and the Welsh kings agree the border at the Wye, removing Cantref Coch (the Forest of Dean); the shape's east edge (2.63 W) already follows the Wye. Morgan ab Owain united Gwent and Glywysing in 942 (Morgan Hen page), so the shape holds 926-941 only. After Gruffydd ap Llywelyn's death Caradog ap Gruffudd re-establishes an independent Gwent under Cadwgan ap Meurig (1063, page); Cliopatria has no Gwent shape after 1055 (Gwynedd's 1056 shape covers it to 1065). The Normans sack parts of Gwent in 1070 and had a castle at Striguil by 1071 (Norman invasion page); the Glywysing page has the Gwent-Glywysing union running to 1074 where this page has Caradog take what remained of Gwent from Cadwgan in 1074. Drawn as the 1046 shape.

region.text: south-east Wales between the Wye and the Usk

ledger.note: 540: Gwent is on the map. The page has the kingdom form after the Roman withdrawal from Britain in the 5th century, with Caradoc, Erb or Tewdrig as uncertain founders; it gives no founding year, so 540 is Cliopatria's start (page silent).

region.text: the Archenfield cell on the Wye added in 577

ledger.note: 577: Cliopatria adds one cell (253 km2) on the Wye in Archenfield. The page says Ergyng and Ewyas were early post-Roman kingdoms that later came under Gwent (no date); the year is Cliopatria's (page silent).

region.text: the Archenfield cell on the Wye

ledger.note: 705: the Archenfield cell leaves Gwent. Cliopatria's Mercia row borders Gwent 661-829; the page dates no loss (page silent).

region.text: Cantref Coch, the Forest of Dean east of the Wye

ledger.note: 926: Athelstan and the Welsh kings fix the border at the Wye. At Hereford, the page says after William of Malmesbury, they agreed the border at the Wye, removing Cantref Coch (the Forest of Dean). Cliopatria's Gwent shape already stops at the Wye, so no cell changes.

region.text: Gwent, joined to Glywysing under Morgan Hen

ledger.note: 942: Morgan Hen unites Gwent and Glywysing as Morgannwg. He 'united the former kingdoms of Gwent and Glywysing in 942 under the name of Morgannwg' (the Gwent infobox: union 942-974). The page also has him submit to Athelstan in 931 and pay 'homage to the English kings as a form of protection': a vassal relation for the England dossier. Cliopatria's union starts in 947.

975: Gwent is separate from Morgannwg again. The Glywysing page: the kingdoms separated again after his death in 974; the Morgan Hen page says only that his son Idwallon died in 975 and Owain followed, and describes no separation. Cliopatria's Gwent shape resumes in 960.

1055: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn takes Gwent. The page: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn wins control of Gwent and Morgannwg, extending his rule over Wales, in 1055; in 1056 he campaigned from near Monmouth and beat Ralph, Earl of Hereford.

1063: Gwent is independent again. After Gruffydd's death Caradog ap Gruffudd re-establishes an independent Gwent under Cadwgan ap Meurig; in 1065 Harold tried to set up a base at Portskewett and Caradog razed it.

region.text: Striguil (Chepstow) and the lower Wye, where the Normans had a castle by 1071

ledger.note: 1070: the Normans sack Gwent. The page: the Normans sack south-east Wales and parts of Gwent in 1070, and Orderic Vitalis places Cadwgan's defeat by William FitzOsbern at the same time; the Norman invasion page has a castle at Striguil by FitzOsbern's death in 1071.

region.text: Striguil (Chepstow) and the lower Wye, where the Normans had a castle by 1071

ledger.note: 1074: Gwent passes to Caradog and the fight with the Normans passes to Morgannwg (the Gwent page has most of Gwent firmly under Norman control when Caradog died in 1081; the Norman invasion page a castle at Caerleon by 1086).
1074: Caradog ap Gruffudd takes what remains of Gwent from Cadwgan ap Meurig; the Glywysing page's infobox has the union 1063-1074 and the name Morgannwg from 1075.

1074: the Kingdom of Gwent ends in Caradog's Morgannwg. The infobox dates the Norman conquest 1070-1090 and the text has the kingdom extinct 'by 1091'; this dossier ends it when Caradog takes control of what remains of Gwent from Cadwgan (1074), and the Normans take the land from Morgannwg.

wars.name: Canute's invasion of Gwent
wars.outcome: Canute invaded Gwent in 1034; the page records no territorial result.

wars.name: Gruffydd ap Llywelyn's conquest of Wales
wars.outcome: Gruffydd won control of Gwent and Morgannwg in 1055; in 1056 he campaigned from near Monmouth and defeated Ralph, Earl of Hereford; after his death in 1063 Caradog ap Gruffudd re-established an independent Gwent.

wars.name: Harold's invasion of Gwent
wars.outcome: Harold of Hereford tried to set up a base at Portskewett and Caradog razed it.

wars.name: Norman invasion of south-east Wales

zones.text: Striguil (Chepstow) and the lower Wye, where the Normans had a castle by 1071

wars.outcome: The Normans sacked south-east Wales and parts of Gwent in 1070 and had a castle at Striguil by 1071; Caradog died in 1081 with most of Gwent firmly under Norman control; Caerleon castle stood by 1086.
wars.note: The Norman invasion page says the attacks 'faltered badly' after Roger de Breteuil forfeited his estates in 1075.

certainty.note: Frontiers are approximate. The one line the page names is the Wye, agreed at Hereford in 926 (the shape's east edge), and it is still drawn soft.

notes: Cliopatria ends Gwent in 1055 (Gruffydd ap Llywelyn); the pages bring it back in 1063 under Caradog ap Gruffudd and end it in 1074 (Gwent page) inside Morgannwg, so the dossier runs to 1074 and adds a 1063-1073 keyframe. The infobox says the Norman conquest ran 1070-1090 and the text 'by 1091'; the Norman invasion page puts a castle at Caerleon by 1086. Disagreement: the Gwent page has an independent Gwent under Cadwgan ap Meurig 1063-1074, the Glywysing page a union of Gwent and Glywysing 1063-1074; this dossier follows the Gwent page. The union 942-974 (Morgan Hen and Gwent pages) is longer than Cliopatria's 947-959; Gwent has no keyframe for 942-974. Vassalage: the Morgan Hen page has Morgan submit to Athelstan in 931 and pay 'homage to the English kings as a form of protection'; the Gwent page has the 931 submission too. Vassal events belong to the overlord's dossier, so the kingdom-of-wessex / kingdom-of-england dossiers should record a vassal_start for kingdom-of-gwent and kingdom-of-morgannwg in 931 (end not dated by any page opened). Pages silent: the 577 and 705 cell changes, the Marcher lordships of Abergavenny, Caerleon, Monmouth and Usk (no dates), the Hwicce and Mercian frontier, the Viking raid of 878-879 that Cliopatria's neighbour list shows. The 1070 contest zone is a 10 km disk at Chepstow because a coarser region would delete 40 percent of the 1,268 km2 shape for one castle. Counterparts needing dossiers: marcher-lordships (Striguil, Caerleon, Monmouth, Abergavenny, Usk). Gazetteer: Gwent, Ergyng/Archenfield, Cantref Coch, Striguil, Caerwent are not in the gazetteer; regions are Cliopatria shapes, a disk and a Chepstow coordinate.
